description: Outline application (Scale and Layout Only) for a two storey front extension, single and two storey side to rear extension (incorporating 3 dormers), single storey rear extension and six dormers within the side and rear roof slope of the house at 147 Eastcote Lane, conversion to form seven self-contained flats. All matters reserved save for scale and layout
decision_conditions:
<ul style="margin-top: 0cm;">
 </ul><p>The applicant has failed to provide any details of
     existing car ownership levels or a parking survey to demonstrate the
     impact the proposed development could have on on-street parking demand for
     a road that already experiences high levels of parking stress due to the absence
     of a controlled parking zone. In the absence of this information, the Local
     Planning Authority cannot be satisfied that the proposal would not result
     in increased pressure on the limited on-street parking available to the detriment
     of existing residents and the safe and efficient operation of the
     surrounding highway network. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policies
     T4 and T6 of the London Plan, Policy CS1 of the Core Strategy and Policy
     DM42 of the Harrow Development Management Policies Local Plan (2013).&nbsp;<o:p></o:p></p><ul style="margin-top: 0cm;">
</ul>

<p class="MsoListParagraph" style="">The
proposal fails to demonstrate how it would achieve the statutory minimum 10%
Biodiversity Net Gain (BNG), as required by the Environment Act 2021. In the
absence of this information, the Local Planning Authority cannot be satisfied
that the development would not result in a net loss of biodiversity or that it
would deliver the required net gain. The proposal is therefore contrary to the
National Planning Policy Framework (2024),&nbsp;Policy G6 of the London Plan
(2021), CS1E of the Harrow Core Strategy (2012) and policies DM20 and DM21
of the Harrow Development Management Policies Local Plan (2013).<o:p></o:p></p>

<p>The proposed development would result in poor quality accommodation that would not be fit for purpose due to the single aspect nature of the flats, inadequate natural ventilation and the potential for overheating, poor outlook from bedroom windows, undersized bedroom, constrained and contrived internal layouts and a lack of high quality, usable outdoor private amenity space, to the detriment of the residential amenities of&nbsp;future occupiers. The proposal would therefore be contrary to the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), Policy D6 of the London Plan (2021), Policy CS1 of the Core Strategy (2012) and Policies&nbsp;DM 1, DM26 and DM27 of the Harrow Development Management Policies Local Plan (2013).</p>
